ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and beneficial owners against the FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) list, United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List, Canadian sanctions administered by Global Affairs Canada, U.S. OFAC SDN List, HM Treasury sanctions, and Canadian Criminal Code anti-terrorism listings. Additionally, ongoing transaction monitoring under PCMLTFA and enhanced due diligence on any PEP, high-risk jurisdiction, or adverse media match.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Registries and Online Services (British Columbia Registrar of Companies); federal alternative: Corporations Canada online filing centre via the Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Name must be in Roman script; if a non-English name is used, a transliterated rendering must be provided that is consistent with Canadian naming conventions; the corporate name must include a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', or 'Incorporated'; French-language names are permissible for provincial BC companies but must meet BC registrar translation and distinctiveness requirements; the name cannot be identical or confusingly similar to any existing BC corporation, extraprovincial company, or federal trademark record; use of numerals as the dominant feature is restricted; punctuation and special characters are limited by the Registrar's administrative policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, a written administrative appeal must be submitted to the Registrar of Companies within 30 days of the rejection notice, under section 28 of the British Columbia Business Corporations Act. The appeal must set out the grounds of distinctiveness and attach a modified NUANS/Name Search report. Alternatively, a new name request may be filed immediately online. An extension of a valid name reservation may be applied for prior to expiry only when the original consent letter supports it; otherwise a fresh name request must be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office in British Columbia is mandatory and must be a physical street address in BC where the company's records are kept and legal process can be served. A virtual office service is acceptable only if it includes a physical BC address and a designated agent to accept service; however, for a manufacturing business (polyhedral dice casting), the virtual office will not satisfy commercial substance requirements and the actual production premises must be maintained separately. Financial institutions will usually insist on a physical operating address.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57, as amended (British Columbia), Part 2 (Incorporation) and applicable regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Registry, Ministry of Citizens' Services, British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) and Notice of Articles (Form 2)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued for such consideration as the directors determine. No escrow or deemed paid-up capital arrangement is required for a non-reporting BC business corporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act is hereby ratified and confirmed, and the Notice of Articles and Articles are adopted as filed. RESOLVED, that the subscription for 1,000 common shares by the founding shareholder be accepted, and that shares be issued upon receipt of lawful consideration in the amount fixed by the board. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be established at [Registered Office Address], British Columbia, and the records office be kept at that address. RESOLVED, that [President Name] be appointed President, [Secretary Name] be appointed Secretary, and [Treasurer Name] be appointed Treasurer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Name Request Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed corporate names through Corporate Online or a registered NUANS search service. Complete the name reservation request, confirm the corporate designation, and retain the Name Reservation Number for use in the incorporation application. The proposed name must be distinguishable from all existing names and not violate trademark or prohibited-name rules.
required_dossiers: Completed BC name reservation request form
NUANS name search report dated within 56 days
Proposed corporate names and corporate designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on availability or public-interest grounds, file a name reconsideration request with the registrar or submit an amended name reservation request with a revised distinguishing element.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Notice of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the online Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, and Articles. Attach the signed consent of each first director. Include the authorized share structure and first directors' full names and addresses. Pay the required filing fee by credit card and submit for statutory review.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice or a query, review the stated defects, correct the application online, and resubmit within the registry-prescribed deadline. If statutory requirements have changed, amend the application to conform before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Certificate of Incorporation and Setting Up Statutory Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registries and Online Services, Corporate Online Dashboard
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation from the Corporate Online portal. Create the company minute book containing the Notice of Articles, Articles, registers of directors, registers of shareholders, and share transfer registers. Arrange a corporate seal only if required by the bylaws.
required_dossiers: Minute book and statutory register templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed or the certificate contains a typographical error, contact the BC Registry contact centre and file the appropriate correction request with proof of the intended particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first directors' meeting or obtain unanimous written consent. Adopt the pro-forma first board resolution approving share subscription, establishment of the registered office, and appointment of officers. Issue share certificates and record all entries in the share register and directors' register.
required_dossiers: Signed first board resolution or unanimous written consent
Share subscription list and payment records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director consent or officer appointment is defective, cure the defect by a subsequent board resolution, obtain unanimous shareholder consent where required, and file any necessary corrected consent with the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax and Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, BC Ministry of Finance, and WorkSafeBC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online to obtain a federal Business Number and register for GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts if applicable. Register for British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax through eTaxBC. Create a WorkSafeBC account and obtain a workplace clearance letter for the operations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registration application is queried, provide the requested supplementary information to CRA, eTaxBC, or WorkSafeBC. Where CRA rejects the GST/HST election, revise the effective date and eligibility details and resubmit the election.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal or Regional District Business Licensing Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation and commencement of premises use, submit a municipal business licence application using the Certificate of Incorporation, lease evidence, floor plan, occupancy load, and insurance certificate. Arrange a fire and building inspection under the BC Fire Code and obtain the municipal business licence before production begins.
required_dossiers: Floor plan and occupancy load calculation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues a deficiency or refuses the licence for zoning or inspection reasons, remedy the stated non-compliance, submit revised plans, and appeal the decision through the municipal business licence review or variance process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Local Municipal or Regional District Business Licensing Department and WorkSafeBC
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence and WorkSafeBC Occupation Health and Safety Clearance

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy / Environmental Assessment Office
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Assessment Certificate for artisan-scale epoxy resin dice casting under the Reviewable Projects Regulation; subject to municipal wastewater and sewer-use authorization and indoor air emission controls under the Environmental Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Volatile organic compounds from epoxy-resin casting must comply with municipal air-quality bylaws and WorkSafeBC exposure limits. Wastewater discharges must not exceed municipal sewer-use bylaw limits for pH, suspended solids, heavy metals, and solvents. Waste epoxy resin and cleaning solvent must be handled as hazardous waste under the BC Hazardous Waste Regulation and disposed of through a licensed carrier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification under the BC Fire Code, including proper storage of flammable epoxy and cleaning agents; structural load review of casting and curing areas; and occupational health and safety clearance from WorkSafeBC under the Workers Compensation Act.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll and excise; Ministry of Finance, British Columbia (BC Consumer Taxation Branch via eTaxBC) — BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) and BC corporate income tax (administered federally by CRA under the Canada–British Columbia Comprehensive Integrated Tax Coordination Agreement). Portal: CRA My Business Account / Business Registration Online (BRO); BC eTaxBC portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A BC Business Corporation must obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or by telephone. Mandatory sequence: (1) file Articles of Incorporation under the BC Business Corporations Act (or the Canada Business Corporations Act with BC extra-provincial registration); (2) obtain the BN; (3) open Income Tax program account RC0001 for T2 corporate tax; (4) open GST/HST program account RT0001 by filing GST1 or through BRO, selecting standard quarterly or annual filing cycle; (5) register separately for BC PST through BC eTaxBC (Form FIN 419) before making any taxable retail sale in BC, as PST has no small-supplier exemption; (6) open Payroll account RP0001 when hiring employees; (7) if the corporation is controlled by non-residents, file the ITA s. 153 information return and, where required, appoint a resident representative under ITA s. 221.2.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian-controlled private corporation eligible for the federal small business deduction — 9% federal rate on active business income up to CAD 500,000 — and the BC small business rate of 11% on the same CAD 500,000 eligible income; resident corporations are taxed on worldwide income under ITA ss. 2, 3 and 250; no US-style pass-through or check-the-box treatment is available; non-resident-owned investment corporations and public corporations are subject to different rate structures).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election. Available elections include: (1) capital cost allowance elections under ITA s. 13 and Schedule II; (2) tax-deferred rollover elections on transfers under ITA s. 85, amalgamations under s. 87, and winding-up under s. 88; (3) Small Business Deduction allocation agreement among associated CCPCs on Form T1009 under ITA s. 125(3); (4) GST/HST elections under ETA s. 211 (closely related corporations) and s. 273 (nil consideration for intercompany taxable supplies); (5) GST/HST Quick Method election under ETA s. 227; (6) fiscal-period election under ITA s. 249.1; (7) where applicable, the s. 216(1) election for non-resident rental income; hybrid mismatch exposure is limited by ITA ss. 18.1 and 18.2, with no domestic hybrid entity election comparable to a check-the-box regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (federal value-added tax at 5%) plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST retail sales/use tax at 7%); combined headline rate of 12% applies to taxable supplies made through a permanent establishment or carrying-on-business presence in British Columbia.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 of gross worldwide taxable supplies (excluding zero-rated exports) measured over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or any single calendar quarter (ETA s. 240(1) small-supplier threshold); once exceeded, mandatory GST/HST registration applies from the month following the excess. PST: no registration threshold — every vendor carrying on business in BC must register with the BC Ministry of Finance before making retail sales, irrespective of revenue. BC Employer Health Tax registration is only required once BC payroll reaches CAD 500,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada operates no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory e-invoicing clearance platform comparable to Brazilian NF-e or Italian SdI. CRA accepts paper, PDF, and any electronic invoice format provided the disclosure rules in ETA s. 221 and GST/HST Information Requirements are satisfied. Registrants with taxable sales above CAD 1.5 million must file GST/HST returns electronically through GST/HST NETFILE within CRA My Business Account; below that threshold, paper filing is permitted. Unless a registrant exits the small-supplier regime, there is no pre-clearance API obligation, but the registrant must preserve complete invoice and export documentation for six years under ETA s. 286 and make them available to CRA on demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Canada are zero-rated under ETA s. 22 where the supplier exports the goods, or delivers them to a common carrier or customs broker for export, within 60 days of the supply (or such longer period as CRA policy permits). Services supplied to non-resident recipients outside Canada, including e-commerce support services for offline tabletop gaming products such as handcrafted epoxy resin liquid-core dice, qualify for zero-rating under ETA Sch. VI Part V s. 7. The exporter must demonstrate delivery outside Canada through a bill of lading, customs export declaration, and contract terms, and must remain able to substantiate a true foreign-resident recipient in order to claim input tax credits and refunds of GST paid on inputs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration filed with CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System / ACI eManifest, where a formal export declaration is required
Bill of Lading (Master or House) or Air Waybill evidencing physical delivery to an overseas consignee
Commercial Invoice annotated as zero-rated export under ETA s. 22 / Sch. VI Part V
Packing List and cargo manifest for the resin dice shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT confirmation, or bank/FX receipt evidencing repatriation of export proceeds in foreign currency
Customs broker instructions or Power of Attorney, if a licensed broker is used
Kickstarter/Stripe or PayPal transaction records, customer shipping addresses, and IP-based evidence establishing non-resident recipient status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess export zero-rating claims within the normal four-year period, which is unlimited where a return was omitted or where misrepresentation, fraud, or willful neglect is established. Failure to retain a valid export documentation bundle recharacterizes the supply as taxable at 5% GST plus 7% PST, giving rise to net tax reassessments, interest, and refund clawbacks of previously credited input tax credits. Civil penalties include: ETA s. 280(1) false statements penalty equal to the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax evaded; s. 285(1) repeated non-compliance penalty; s. 280(2) failure to file or remit penalty; statutory interest charged at the prescribed rate (2025 annual rate 9%, compounded daily) on all unremitted and clawed-back amounts; and penalties for failure to keep books and records under ITA s. 238. Where an exporter knowingly fabricates bills of lading or inward remittance certificates, criminal tax evasion charges may be laid under ETA s. 327(1) and ITA s. 239, exposing the corporation to fines in addition to any evaded tax and, for directors and officers who directed the fraud, imprisonment of up to five years. Clawback adjustments must be reported as a debit to net tax in the period in which reassessed and disclosed in the corresponding T2 corporate income tax filings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as central monetary authority; formal exchange control administration is not a standalone agency under Canadian law. Operational FX oversight is distributed among the Global Affairs trade finance directorate, the Canada Border Services Agency for cross-border currency reporting obligations, and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for regulated financial institutions. The Governor of the Bank of Canada does not pre-authorise commercial FX transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Both capital and current account transactions are fully convertible in Canada. The Canadian dollar floats freely with no exchange-control permits, no surrender requirements, and no limitations on profit remittance by a non-resident shareholder. The only practical hurdles are indirect: (i) outgoing dividends are subject to Part XIII withholding tax at 25% or a treaty-reduced rate, and (ii) the receiving Canadian bank must complete standard AML and tax-identification formalities before wiring funds abroad. For the target business of digital tabletop gaming dice sales, bank transfer payments or crowdfunding payouts by Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal may be treated as current-account receipts and are freely convertible into CAD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose statutory timelines or mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts. An exporting British Columbia corporation may retain and use foreign-currency proceeds without a requirement to repatriate or convert them into CAD. Any receipt is nonetheless reportable for GST/HST and income tax, and for foreign exchange gains/losses, under the Income Tax Act and applicable CRA compliance forms.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, with legal restraint. Canada does not issue an EU-style electronic money institution (EMI) licence; an entity accepting deposits must be a federally regulated bank or be supervised by OSFI. Offshore digital EMIs are acceptable only as non-deposit payment facilitators (PSP-like vendors) and cannot operate as the primary treasury account for an escrow in British Columbia. A local Schedule I bank account remains mandatory for capital escrow, corporate identity, and tax reporting. If a fintech rail such as Wise/Payoneer or Stripe Treasury is used, the Canadian entity must register as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC, appoint a Canadian compliance officer, adopt a written AML/CFT program, and report large cross-border electronic funds transfers (over CAD 10,000).
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and beneficial owners are generally required to attend an in-person KYC interview at a Canadian branch for initial corporate account opening. Physical presence is strongly mandated by most Schedule I banks for a crowdfunding-led business and for foreign shareholders. Remote video opening is possible only where the individual has already established banking relations, passes a notarised identity verification, or the bank uses a certified remote-onboarding module; however, the PCMLTFA KYC record must include a reliable verification of the person’s identity and full beneficial ownership. For this BC corporation with a new activity, plan for at least one director to appear in person with governing corporate documents, Business Number confirmation, and a physical BC address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner opacity: a non-resident shareholder or layered corporate structure concealing ultimate owner income during crowdfunding account opening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate ofContinuous Record; articles of incorporation? At minimum provide 6-month board minutes, register of directors, register of shareholders, beneficial ownership declaration signed by all ultimate owners, passport and proof of address for each person with 25%+ equity, source-of-wealth statement for the subscription funds, and any amalgamation or name-change certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk crowdfunding inflow mismatch: Kickstarter and PayPal settlements show many small incoming payment credits inconsistent with the low-value physical goods profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Kickstarter campaign funding receipt, price list of polyhedral dice sets, shipping manifests, customer order logs, Stripe/PayPal transaction settlement reports, refund policy, proof of purchase of resin/dice moulds, and a board resolution explaining the purpose and source of each batch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign jurisdiction nexus: funds originating from offshore platforms or payment hubs without clear trade or e-commerce documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreement with Kickstarter and payment providers, Stripe/PayPal merchant account onboarding evidence, e-store domain evidence, terms of sale, customer geographic report, supplier invoices for dice accessories, evidence of BC warehouse or fulfilment contract, and tax numbers for GST and income tax.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential structuring or third-party mediation: payments received from one entity but paid to multiple small overseas suppliers with frequent wire transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply chain contracts with each resin/packaging supplier, shipping bills of lading or courier manifests, goods-in records, payment invoices, bank wire instructions and beneficiary verification, employee or contractor agreements for the dice polishing process, and quarterly treasury cash-flow forecasting files.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contribution by a non-resident shareholder is executed by wire transfer from the offshore bank to the BC entity’s Canadian bank account. The remittance should use SWIFT MT103 with an OECD-BPM6 clear purpose code, e.g. 'equity investment (521)' or 'capital contribution to trading operation'. The receiving Canadian bank must be informed via a deposit slip note or secured transactional reference such as 'ISSUANCE OF SHARES' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN'. A board resolution approving the share subscription or intercompany loan must be kept on file along with the subscriber’s source-of-funds documentation. Because Canada has no FX allocation or exchange control approval, the only execution hurdles are completion of the bank’s legal-entity identification and AML checks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For global consumer sales, the primary rail is the Stripe/PayPal settlement of crowdfunding and webstore payouts direct to the Canadian CAD account. For international trade with resin suppliers, beading agent and packaging houses, the standard rail is a Canadian bank international wire in SWIFT MT103 / MT202 COV with a transaction purpose code such as 'supplier payment to a resin manufacturer' or 'advance import payment'. For larger and repeat supplier invoices, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued in MT700 under the ICC UCP600 can be used; the BC company’s bank advises the LC via the supplier’s correspondent bank, with the issuing bank still on the hook for final payment. CAD/USD contingent hedging is best executed via the treasury desk of the main cash-maintaining bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (outright USD/CAD puts and calls) for firm trade settlement obligations up to 12 months
Spot-deferred forwards for commodity-linked supplier purchases with an optional delivery window

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) limited to exotic currencies where Canadian financial institutions may quote a CAD-settled NDF; used cautiously and evidenced under an ISDA International Swaps and Derivatives Association master agreement
Cross-currency swaps (plain-vanilla fixed/float) between CAD and USD for term debt or committed capital expenditures
FX options on major cross rates when approved by the bank’s market limits, with premium paid up front and no negative cycles on the balance sheet

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registry – Corporate Registry, Ministry of Finance (via BC Registries Online)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary date of incorporation, amalgamation, or restoration (e.g., incorporated March 15 -> due by May 14 each year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 100 (approx. USD 73) applies after the 2-month deadline; two consecutive missed annual reports authorize the Registrar to dissolve the company under the BC Business Corporations Act

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if the company is a reporting issuer, distributes securities to the public, or if shareholders holding at least 5% of issued shares validly resolve to appoint an auditor. Otherwise, audit can be waived by unanimous shareholder resolution under BCBCA Part 11.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public (reporting) issuers; Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook (ASPE) for private enterprises; annual financial statements must be prepared in accordance with the applicable framework and retained for CRA audit purposes

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the BC Transparency Register rules, the company must maintain and annually review an internal register of individuals with significant control (ISC). Shareholders must notify the company of any significant-control changes within 14 days of acquiring or ceasing control, and the register must be made available to enforcement authorities upon request. No separate annual government filing is required for private companies unless a prescribed event occurs.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders and Directors Meetings
Transparency Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 3,700–11,000 (CAD 5,000–15,000) for a small private manufacturing company

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27.0% combined headline rate (federal 15.0% + British Columbia general provincial rate 12.0%); reduced combined rate of 10.0% (federal 9.0% + BC 1.0%) applies to Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) active business income up to CAD 500,000 gross per year
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays in British Columbia. Effective incentives: CCPC Small Business Deduction (combined 10.0% on first CAD 500,000 of active business income); Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) refundable investment tax credits up to 35% of qualified expenditures for CCPCs; capital cost allowance (CCA) accelerated deductions on manufacturing and processing equipment; non-capital loss carryforward of 20 years and carryback of 3 years is statutorily available, though the compliance template records a 5-year carryforward limitation for model consistency

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return — filed electronically through the CRA BizStatements corporate tax e-file portal; British Columbia provincial tax is integrated via Schedule T2S63 filed with the T2
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; each fiscal period ends on any permitted month-end; T2 must be filed once per fiscal year
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 filing deadline is six (6) months after fiscal year-end; final balance-due tax is payable two (2) months after year-end (three (3) months for an eligible CCPC); quarterly instalments are due on the 15th day of March, June, September and December when prior-year federal and provincial tax payable exceeds CAD 3,000

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: legal name, CRA business number (BN/RT), jurisdiction of incorporation, fiscal period start and end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Canadian branch address in care of the authorized representative; if incorporated outside Canada, select the non-resident corporation indicator and attach the BC permanent establishment allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue: total sales of sharp-edge epoxy resin liquid-core RPG dice, Kickstarter pre-sale proceeds net of platform fees, PayPal/Stripe merchant receipts, shipping surcharges, and incidental licensing income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source gross revenues attributable to the British Columbia permanent establishment; exclude foreign-source revenues unless they are treaty-allocated to Canada.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total deductible expenses: cost of goods sold (resin, molds, pigments, sharp-edge castings, packaging), subcontract labour, Kickstarter/Stripe/PayPal processing fees, freight and customs, rent, utilities, wages, professional fees, and CCA claims.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct either actual expenses directly incurred by the BC PE or a reasonable apportionment of head-office expenses under section 4 of the Income Tax Act; unreasonable allocations are disregarded and adjusted by the CRA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: net income after reserves, capital gains/losses, loss carryovers, and non-taxable dividends; includes adjustments for prepaid crowdfunding deposits recognized as income when the risk of refund is substantially extinguished.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations with a PE in Canada compute taxable income on the same base but must separate Canadian-source business income; the three-year carryback and twenty-year carryforward of non-capital losses applies to the Canadian PE only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal basic tax payable: 38% of taxable income minus: 10% provincial abatement, 13% general rate reduction, and 28% small business reduction on the qualified active business income of a CCPC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation is generally not entitled to the 10% provincial abatement unless the income is allocated to a Canadian province; use the only the federal base rate thresholds applicable to the PE income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: British Columbia taxable income and provincial corporation tax calculation: BC allocation percentage for multi-jurisdiction corporations and the BC small business deduction (1% rate on eligible active business income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the BC allocation schedule; if the corporation has a PE only in BC, allocate 100% of Canadian taxable income to BC; if multiple PEs exist, use the uniform statutory apportionment formula.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule 200 / S3 capital gains and T2S63-A
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting net income to taxable income; segregates active business income, property income, dividends, taxable capital gains, and allowable capital losses; reports reserves under GIF and contingency rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert branch tax computation when the non-resident corporation distributes PE income; a 25% branch tax under Part XIV applies on BC PE taxable income less reinvestment allowances and treaty credits, unless exempted by a tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory cross-border information return disclosing not-at-arm's-length transactions with non-residents; captures product sales, IP licensing, management fees, and intercompany payment flows for dice casting, mould design, and resin procurement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the non-resident counterparty's legal name, country of residence, tax identification number, transaction codes, and the arm's length method applied (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, or profit split).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late T2 filing penalty: 5% of the unpaid tax balance, plus 1% per full month of continued non-filing (maximum 12 months, i.e., up to 17% of the unpaid balance); even with zero balance due, failure to file on time is penalized up to CAD 1,000 (reduced to CAD 100 after three years); prescribed-rate interest (compound daily, reset quarterly) is charged on all unpaid instalments and balance-due amounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2S63 — British Columbia Corporation Tax Calculation Schedule; filed as an integrated component of the T2 through the CRA BizStatements e-file portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; filed with the T2 for each fiscal period
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within six (6) months of fiscal year-end; the BC balance is payable with the federal balance-due date (two months after year-end, or three months for eligible CCPCs)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Multi-jurisdiction apportionment of taxable income between British Columbia and other provinces or territories based on statutory payroll and gross revenue factors.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with only a BC permanent establishment enters 100%; corporations with several PEs complete the BC prescribed allocation formula and attach supporting payroll and revenue schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: BC 1% small business rate applied to the corporation's active business income earned in BC up to the annual CAD 500,000 business limit; rate increase recaptures the deduction over the federal small business threshold.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations are not eligible for the BC small business deduction; any positive BC income is taxed at the 12% general BC rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: BC provincial corporation tax at 12% computed on BC taxable income after the small business deduction and non-capital loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This line concludes the BC provincial tax obligation; treaty relief under the Canada-BC jurisdiction cannot reduce the provincial rate, but foreign tax credits are claimed on the federal return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: BC penalties are administered in the federal T2 assessment; failure to file or late filing of the T2S63 triggers the same 5% plus 1% monthly late-filing penalty on the BC provincial portion, with interest compounded daily at the prescribed rate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T106 Information Return for Non-Arm's Length Transactions with Non-Residents; filed through CRA's My Business internet service or as an XML attachment to the T2
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; required where cross-border non-arm's length transactions exceed CAD 1,000,000 with any single non-resident in the fiscal period
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due with the T2 return within six (6) months after fiscal year-end; the filing obligation applies even if no tax is payable

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part II — transaction codes and amounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Codes designating the nature and quantum of each non-arm's length payment or receipt: sales of goods, royalties for IP, management and administrative fees, interest, and cost recharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the non-resident entity's jurisdiction and tax treaty status; also report deemed dividends or branch distributions where relevant.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selected arm's length method (CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM, or profit split) and an explanation of comparability adjustments for the dice manufacturing value chain.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the method applied to the Canadian legal entity's intercompany flows; attach a brief functional and risk analysis sufficient to support the selected method.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file T106 on time attracts CAD 100 per month per return, capped at CAD 1,000 per year; if the failure is made knowingly or in circumstances amounting to gross negligence, penalties escalate to CAD 1,000 per month, capped at CAD 5,000, plus interest; the CRA may also reopen the statute-barred period where a T106 is omitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: NR4 Tax Withheld by Payers for Non-Residents; filed electronically via CRA's internet file transfer service, with the annual NR4 Summary
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual calendar-year reporting, regardless of the corporation's fiscal year-end; quarterly payments of withheld non-resident tax are due by the 15th day following each calendar quarter
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: NR4 slips and NR4 Summary must be filed by February 28 of the following calendar year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts paid to non-residents: Box 16 dividends, Box 17 interest, Box 18 royalties, Box 19 rental payments, and Box 22 pension or other payments; the corresponding amount withheld at source is recorded in the adjacent tax-withheld boxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Form NR301-A (Statement by a Non-Resident Claiming Treaty Benefits) to support each reduced treaty withholding rate; do not apply treaty rates without the beneficiary owner's valid tax residency certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name, address, country of residence, and foreign tax identification number of the non-resident payee; also indicate beneficial ownership status and whether the payee is a corporation, individual, or transparent partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation claiming reduced withholding must certify its status as a resident of the relevant treaty country and confirm it is the beneficial owner of the income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold: 10% of the required withheld amount; knowing or intentional failure: 20% of the required withholding; unpaid amounts attract the prescribed daily compound interest; CRA can recover the full gross withholding amount from the Canada-based payer, plus penalties and interest, even if the withholding was never deducted from the payee.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25.0% on dividends paid or credited to non-residents under subsection 212(2) of the Income Tax Act; the rate is reduced under applicable tax treaties (e.g., 5% for a substantial corporate shareholder under the Canada-US treaty, 10% under the Canada-China treaty, and 15% for portfolio shareholders under most Canadian DTAs)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Administrative protocol: (1) confirm treaty entitlement by determining the recipient's residence under the relevant double tax agreement (DTA) and verifying beneficial ownership; (2) obtain Form NR301-A (Statement by a Non-Resident Claiming Treaty Benefits) and a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the foreign tax authority; (3) submit the TRC and NR301-A to the Canadian paying corporation before the payment date; (4) the Canadian payer withholds at the treaty-reduced rate and files the NR4 return; (5) if treaty relief was unavailable at source, the non-resident can claim a refund of excess withholding by filing Form NR7-R with the CRA within two years of the end of the calendar year in which the tax was withheld; (6) the CRA may also issue an advance treaty ruling or letter from its International and Large Business Directorate confirming the applicable rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding: 25.0% on royalties, 25.0% on interest, except interest payable to arm's length lenders is generally exempt from Part XIII withholding under section 212(3)(b); treaty rates typically reduce interest and royalties to 10% (e.g., Canada-China, Canada-UK and Canada-Germany treaties); US interest is usually exempt or reduced to 0-10% depending on the instrument and exemptions under the Canada-US treaty, and US royalties on IP are ordinarily reduced to 10%; for the tabletop RPG dice business, licensing payments for mould designs, trademark use, and resin formulation IP to foreign licensors are subject to the same 25% statutory royalty withholding and qualify for treaty reductions only where a valid TRC is in place

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canadian transfer-pricing rules under subsection 247(4) require contemporaneous documentation to be prepared and filed within three months after the CRA requests it; the statutory T106 disclosure is mandatorily filed when non-arm's length transactions with a single non-resident exceed CAD 1,000,000; a Local File is expected by CRA practice where related-party transactions with any one non-resident exceed CAD 1,000,000, and a Master File is generally expected for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of CAD 10,000,000 or more; Country-by-Country reporting applies where consolidated group revenue is CAD 1.1 billion or more; for the present dice manufacturing operation, a prudent Local File should be maintained even below these thresholds using CUP benchmark prices for raw resin procurement and end-product comparables
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime in the manner of zero-tax jurisdictions, but economic substance is constitutionally enforced through: (1) the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under section 245 of the Income Tax Act; (2) the foreign accrual property income (FAPI) rules under sections 91-95; (3) the arm's length transfer-pricing rules under section 247; and (4) CRA's audit doctrine under Information Circular IC 87-2R; a BC-incorporated dice manufacturer must maintain demonstrable substance in British Columbia — physical premises, employees engaged in mould design, casting, quality control, fulfilment and billing — and cannot channel profits to a zero-tax haven without meaningful people functions, assets, and risk assumption; the CRA will re-characterize intercompany agreements that lack commercial plausibility and allocate income to the jurisdiction where the core value-creating activities actually occur

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Kickstarter pre-sale revenue, PayPal and Stripe settlement income, or cash sales from the T2 return; fabricating supplier invoices to inflate cost of goods sold; claiming fictitious SR&ED expenditures or capital cost allowance on non-existent equipment; providing false documentation during a CRA audit of sharp-edge epoxy dice sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty under subsection 163(2): 50% of the understated tax or overclaimed credits, plus prescribed daily compound interest; criminal conviction under section 239 of the Income Tax Act: fine of 100% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to 5 years; the CRA may also revoke the corporation's GST/HST registration and reassess any statute-barred year where misrepresentation is established.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and controlling officers who knowingly participate in filing a false return face personal criminal liability with sentences of up to 5 years of imprisonment; the CRA can issue assessment against the individual under subsection 160(1) for transfers of property made to defeat tax claims, issue garnishment and asset-freezing orders, and impose travel bans through court orders or immigration hold proceedings when the accused is a non-citizen or at risk of leaving Canada.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty Shopping Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a British Columbia corporation with no real operational substance while all casting, shipping, and marketing functions are performed by an offshore affiliate; placing valuable IP such as resin formula, mold designs, or brand trademarks into a zero-tax intermediary; charging inflated royalties to the Canadian manufacturing entity to strip taxable profit out of Canada; using a conduit entity solely to claim treaty benefits on dividends or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR denies the tax benefit and re-characterizes the arrangement based on economic substance; CRA reallocates income to the Canadian entity under section 247 and imposes 25% Part XIII withholding on deemed dividends or royalties; a 25% branch tax under Part XIV can be applied if the substance is found in Canada through a foreign enterprise; administrative monetary penalties under the Income Tax Act and the Excise Tax Act may also apply for false schedules submitted in relation to the shell arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face joint and several liability for the reassessed corporate tax, withholding shortfalls, and penalties; in egregious cases, criminal charges under section 380 of the Criminal Code for fraud can result in imprisonment; the BC Registrar can issue a dissolution order for a shell corporation failing to demonstrate BC substance; individuals may be barred from re-entering Canada and subject to international arrest notices where fraud or money laundering is connected to the shell structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately structuring cash or electronic deposits into multiple tranches below CAD 10,000 to avoid FINTRAC large cash transaction reports; laundering proceeds from crowdfunding fraud through shell payment accounts; accepting anonymous cryptocurrency payments for dice sets and converting them to fiat without applying customer due diligence; falsely classifying suspicious third-party remittances as 'pre-orders' or 'donations'; failing to maintain a compliance program after exceeding FINTRAC registration thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: up to CAD 500,000 per contravention for corporations and CAD 100,000 per contravention for individuals; criminal recourse under the Criminal Code for laundering proceeds of crime leads to fines of up to CAD 1,000,000 and imprisonment of up to 10 years; the CRA may also apply gross negligence penalties of up to CAD 100,000 on unreported foreign-source income connected to the laundering activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners face personal administrative penalties for failing to implement FINTRAC controls; conviction for laundering offences exposes individuals to up to 10 years of imprisonment; courts may impose travel bans, asset freezes, and forfeiture orders; Fusion-centre investigations frequently lead to non-resident directors being denied Canadian entry and to extradition proceedings for related fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to a non-resident shareholder, royalties to a foreign IP licensor, interest to a non-resident lender, or management fees to an offshore associate without withholding the statutory 25% Part XIII tax; failing to obtain a valid tax residency certificate and then applying a treaty rate without entitlement; omitting NR4 slips and summaries; routing payments through treaty-favourable jurisdictions without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty under subsection 227(8) of the Income Tax Act: 10% of the amount required to be withheld if the failure was not deliberate, rising to 20% if the failure was made knowingly or under circumstances amounting to gross negligence; the CRA also charges daily compound interest on the unremitted amounts; the tax, penalties, and interest are recoverable from the Canadian corporation; where a person transfers assets to avoid payment, section 160 assessments attach to the transferee.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the unremitted non-resident withholding tax under section 227.1, irrespective of whether the corporation itself can pay; the CRA must issue a liability notice within two years after the director ceases office, but the collection remedies extend to the director's personal assets; in fraudulent cases, directors can face criminal sanction and imprisonment; travel bans and passport seizures are available to compel attendance and prevent dissipation before judgment; the corporation's BC registrar may also refuse to issue a certificate of good standing until the withholding obligations are discharged.
